author: opt-B1

contract.sync_assumed: caller separates consecutive calls that reuse the temp storage by a block barrier
contract.sync_performed: __syncthreads inside: 2 per radix pass plus 1 init plus 3 in the pairs exchange epilogue
contract.k_range: [1, N) at run time, k == N returns the input unchanged
contract.n_range: N = 256 x IPT, IPT >= 1, measured 1024 to 32768 (the exchange buffer of N x 4 bytes is dynamic shared memory)
contract.type_constraints: fp32 and bf16 through the radix traits, int32 indices
contract.nan_behavior: NaN twiddles to the largest radix key and is selected first, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 is normalized to +0.0 for ranking
contract.tie_break_support: not supported in this variant: ties at the k-th key are resolved by shared-memory atomic ticket order (not_guaranteed only). B1_det carries the warp-redundant rank
contract.sorted_output_support: not supported inherently, post-sort of k

low_level: Same pass machinery as B1_reference (the striped branch header c7cf73b09d copied into approaches/B1/block_topk_air_striped.cuh): identical BAR.SYNC counts (25 bf16, 37 fp32 in the latency kernel), 1 to 6 percent fewer SASS instructions (704 against 736 at N 1024 bf16, 12184 against 12584 at N 32768 k 256 bf16) because the striped slot arithmetic folds into the item loop and E2 drops the loop-carried total_selected. Registers 36 to 38 against 40 to 44 at IPT 4 (throughput kernel 32 against 32 bf16, 32 against 38 fp32, occupancy 8 against 6 blocks per SM for fp32), equal at IPT 16 and 64, and 255 with 216 to 248 bytes of spill against 992 to 1024 bytes (fp32) or 0 bytes (bf16) at IPT 128.

The striped harness load (one 2 or 4 byte load per item, coalesced by construction) costs about the same generate-only control as the vectorized blocked load at N 1024 (139 cycles) and N 4096 bf16 (254 against 271), but 517 to 580 against 904 to 919 at N 4096 fp32 and 3.5k to 3.8k against 4.6k to 8.7k at N 32768, so the subtraction leaves less uncertainty on the striped side at large N.

Temp storage is identical (4128 bytes plus the N x 4 byte exchange buffer), the striped histogram option is the identity at 256 threads with 256 bins (one bin per thread), so this variant measures the arrangement and E2 only.
algorithmic: In the latency regime the striped arrangement is within 3 percent of the blocked reference at N 1024 (1880 against 1882 bf16 k 16, 2017 against 2038 fp32 k 64), 1 to 7 percent slower at N 4096 fp32 k 16 and 64 (3971 against 3704, 4854 against 4671) and 3 to 18 percent faster where k is large or N is 32768 (bf16 N 4096 k 1024 4896 against 5767, fp32 N 32768 k 1024 30720 against 36124). The large-k gain is the epilogue: the gather of the first k slots is item-major in striped order, so at k 1024 and IPT 16 every thread gathers 4 consecutive slots instead of threads 0 to 63 gathering 16 each, and the same holds for the scatter conflicts.

In the throughput regime striped wins every cell, 3 to 7 percent at N 1024, 5 to 30 percent at N 4096 and 6 to 31 percent at N 32768, with the largest gains at the largest k (fp32 N 4096 k 1024 382 against 293 Gelem per s). The occupancy gain for fp32 at N 1024 (8 against 6 blocks per SM) contributes at that size, elsewhere the occupancy is equal and the gain is the cheaper exchange and the lower spill traffic at IPT 128.

bf16 and fp32 cost the same within a few percent at N 1024 (two 8-bit passes without early exit against two to four with it), as on the reference card. The host simulation (approaches/B1/sim_passes.md section 1) gives the pass count distribution behind this: on random normal input the fp32 8-bit schedule executes 2 passes in 56 to 73 percent of the rows at N 1024 and in only 5 to 28 percent at N 32768 (mean 2.94 passes at k 256, 3.02 at k 2048), and bf16 8+8 executes 2 passes in 97 to 100 percent of the rows.
negative: The striped arrangement is not a latency win by itself at the focus sizes: at N 4096 fp32 k 16 it is 7 percent slower than blocked in the latency regime (3971 against 3704) while 7 percent faster in throughput. Its value in the agent (knowledge base 4.3) came from removing the shared-memory transposes, which the harness does not model, so the arrangement is kept as the baseline for the agent's sake, not for a harness gain.
surprises: At IPT 128 the striped header spills for bf16 (255 registers, 248 bytes of spill in the latency kernel) where the blocked reference does not (254 registers, 0 bytes), and still measures 3 to 11 percent faster. For fp32 the striped header spills a quarter of what the blocked one does (232 against 992 bytes).

The generate-only control of the striped load at N 4096 fp32 is 40 percent cheaper than the vectorized blocked load (517 against 904 cycles per call), so a raw-slope comparison would have shown a larger striped gain than the net one.
open_questions: Where exactly do the 7 percent at N 4096 fp32 k 16 go in the latency regime? The pass count is the same (37 barriers), the SASS is 8 instructions shorter, so the suspect is the bank pattern of the striped gather of the first k slots at small k (threads 0 to 15 gather one slot each, 16 slots in 16 banks) against the blocked gather (4 threads gather 4 consecutive slots each).

Does the bf16 spill at IPT 128 come from the memoized key copy (IPT registers of 16-bit keys that the compiler keeps in 32-bit registers) and does the index-only variant without memoization remove it?

correctness_notes: 22 cells, 13 oracle cases each (4 random seeds plus the 9-pattern battery), all passed. prefer_smaller_index not supported by this variant and not run.
